newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee plummets on talk of stock build up.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee plummets on talk of stock build up.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures tumbled on Thursday as commodity funds sold heavy amid talk of a sharp increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks during the month of March, traders said.

Most-active May delivery plunged 15.45 cents per lb -- or about eight percent -- on the day, to 177.70 cents, after ranging from 190.50 to 177.00. Second-month July dropped 11.90 cents to 163.35 cents while the back months finished down 1.70 to 10.65.

Traders said lackluster demand at Brazil's monthly auction on Wednesday also weighed on sentiment. Brazil's government sold a total of 128,660 60-kg bags, or 39.44 percent of the 326,188 bags offered in the auction.
"There is disappointment over the auctions in Brazil, " one trader said. "And it appears traders are looking for GCA stocks to be up sharply."

Rumors swirled around the floor on Thursday that the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly data, slated for release on April 15, would show an increase of up to a whopping one million 60-kg bags in March.
In February, by comparison, GCA coffee stocks rose by 204,000 bags to 1,546,000 bags. In March 1996, U.S. consumer coffee stocks increased by 151,000 bags to 2,372,000 bags, the GCA reported.

"I think it is plausible GCA stocks will be up sharply," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "Overall coffee exports are well above this time last year, so it is not surprising to me that the market is not absorbing all the coffee coming in."

Traders and analysts said the recent surge in CSCE future prices -- which reached their highest level in 2-1/2 years in early March -- had inspired record shipments during February and March from many Latin American producers looking to take advantage of attractively high prices.
However, Prendergast and other analysts said the increase in the U.S. coffee stocks was likely to be closer to 500,000 bags, rather than one million bags.
"One million seems rather large," Prendergast said. "I think 500,000 is more possible unless there was a substantial downturn in consumption."
Additionally, analysts pointed out that a good deal of the recent Latin American coffee exports were sent to European roasters.
"So much of the shipments were destined for Europe," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "I can't see how we are going to have a one million-bag build in the U.S."
While a stock buildup would calm supply worries in the near-term, many analysts warned the tight supply situation was far from over.
"It may be a short-term easing of supply concerns, but the gravy train has stopped," Ganes said. "The problem is: what happens after April when you have a slowdown in shipments."
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 250 60-kg bags to 83,078 60-kg bags as of April 2. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume reached an estimated 15,774 lots, up slightly from Wednesday's official tally of 14,169 lots.
